comparison: Perfect agreement on C91. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers support that bidirectional transcriptional changes (loss of neuronal genes, gain of non-neuronal genes) explain loss of neuronal identity and function with age.

Perfect agreement on C95. Both recognize these as novel discoveries linking specific genes to cognitive aging, with peer reviewers emphasizing the discovery of novel regulators of learning and memory.

Perfect agreement on C110-C112. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers affirm the dataset's value as a resource, with peer reviewers noting it adds to existing datasets by providing transcriptomes of older animals and demonstrating benefits of tissue-specific RNA-seq.

Strong agreement on C65-C68. Both support the functional validation showing that knockdown of daf-2-upregulated genes impairs learning and memory in daf-2 worms, implicating specific neuronal transcriptional targets in maintaining cognitive ability. OpenEval also addresses C76 which peer reviewers include in R10.

Strong agreement on C28-C32 regarding FACS methodology. Both praise the neuron-specific approach, with peer reviewers calling it 'cutting-edge' and emphasizing the importance of cell-specific deep sequencing. OpenEval also addresses C26-C27 which peer reviewers evaluate separately in R1.

Agreement on C33-C35 regarding loss of neuronal identity genes with age. Both accept the differential expression findings and GO analysis. Peer reviewers also address C39 and C41 (specific neuronal markers) which OpenEval evaluates in R9.

Agreement on C55-C57 regarding extended learning and memory in daf-2 mutants. Both support the behavioral findings and daf-16 dependence. Peer reviewers also address C69 (proportional extension) which OpenEval evaluates separately in R15. OpenEval also addresses C58 which peer reviewers evaluate separately in R12.

Agreement on C61-C63 regarding stress-resistance gene program in daf-2 neurons. Both affirm the finding, though OpenEval notes caution about functional inference from orthologs. Peer reviewers also address C72 and C78 which OpenEval evaluates separately in R20 and R23.

Agreement on C73-C76 regarding tissue-specific regulation and value of neuron-specific analysis. Peer reviewers particularly praise the dod-24 example showing differences between whole-body and neuron-specific profiles. Peer reviewers also address C107-C109 which OpenEval evaluates separately in R35-R36.

Agreement on C47-C48 regarding upregulation of proteolysis and epigenetic regulators with age. Both accept these findings as indicating dysregulation. Peer reviewers also address C70-C71 (bidirectional changes) which OpenEval evaluates separately in R19.

Agreement on C53-C54 regarding deleterious effects of age-upregulated genes. Both support that knockdown improves memory in young animals. Peer reviewers also address C52 and C92 which OpenEval evaluates separately in R12 and R26.

Agreement on C117-C120 regarding active resilience mechanisms in daf-2. Both accept that daf-2 uses distinct mechanisms from young wild-type worms. OpenEval notes the interpretation is somewhat speculative. Peer reviewers also address C77, C96, C104, C116 which OpenEval evaluates in R22 and R29.

Agreement on C93 regarding individual gene effects on memory being distinct from longevity pathways. Both accept the functional validation experiments. Peer reviewers also address C94 which OpenEval does not explicitly evaluate separately.

Agreement on C101-C102 regarding additional transcription factors beyond DAF-16. Both accept the comparative analyses showing small differences between N2 and daf-2;daf-16 neurons. Peer reviewers also address C100 and C103 which OpenEval evaluates separately in R33.

Agreement on C26-C27 regarding timepoint selection for cognitively aged worms. Both support the Day 7-8 timepoint, with peer reviewers calling it 'elegantly chosen.' OpenEval evaluates this together with C28-C32 in R7, while peer reviewers evaluate timepoint selection separately from methodology.

Agreement on C69 regarding proportional extension of cognitive function relative to lifespan in daf-2. Both support this finding. Peer reviewers evaluate this together with C55-C57 in R6, while OpenEval evaluates it separately in R15.

Agreement on C92 regarding age-upregulated genes being deleterious rather than compensatory. Both support that knockdown in young animals improves memory. Peer reviewers evaluate this together with C52-C54 in R5, while OpenEval evaluates it separately in R26.

Agreement on C100 regarding tissue-specific analysis revealing neuron-specific regulatory changes. Both accept the comparative analyses. Peer reviewers evaluate this together with C101-C103 in R16, while OpenEval evaluates it separately in R33.

Partial overlap on C39 and C41 regarding specific neuronal markers declining with age. Both support these findings. Peer reviewers evaluate these together with C33-C35 in R3, while OpenEval evaluates them together with C36-C41 in R9.

Partial overlap on C72 regarding stress response and homeostasis genes in daf-2. Both support this as a plausible mechanism. Peer reviewers evaluate this together with C61-C63 and C78 in R7, while OpenEval evaluates it separately in R20.

Partial overlap on C78 regarding conservation of neuroprotective function in mammalian orthologs. Both support this finding. Peer reviewers evaluate this together with C61-C63 and C72 in R7, while OpenEval evaluates it separately in R23.

Partial overlap on C52 regarding utx-1 knockdown improving memory. Both support this finding. Peer reviewers evaluate this together with C53-C54 and C92 in R5, while OpenEval evaluates it together with C49-C52 in R12.

Partial overlap on C96 regarding age-specific mechanisms in daf-2. Both support that Day 8 genes are distinct from Day 1 genes. Peer reviewers evaluate this together with C77, C104, C116-C120 in R9, while OpenEval evaluates it separately in R29.

Partial overlap on C77, C104, C116 regarding age-specific transcriptional programs. Both support comparison with Day 1 data showing distinct mechanisms. Peer reviewers evaluate these together with C96 and C117-C120 in R9, while OpenEval evaluates them separately in R22.

Partial overlap on C70-C71 regarding bidirectional changes explaining cognitive decline. Both support this interpretation. Peer reviewers evaluate this together with C47-C48 in R4, while OpenEval evaluates it separately in R19.

Partial overlap on C58 regarding mechanistic distinction between learning and memory. Both support the differential effects in daf-16;daf-2 mutants. Peer reviewers evaluate this separately in R12, while OpenEval evaluates it together with C55-C58 in R14.

Partial overlap on C108-C109 regarding neuron-specific upregulation. Both support the inference from comparing whole-worm and neuron data. Peer reviewers evaluate this together with C73-C76 and C107 in R10, while OpenEval evaluates it separately in R36.

Partial overlap on C107 regarding neuron-autonomous function. Both support tissue-specificity arguments. Peer reviewers evaluate this together with C73-C76 and C108-C109 in R10, while OpenEval evaluates it together with C105-C107 in R35.

OpenEval supports C79-C83 and C121 regarding mechanistic context for utx-1 effects on memory. These are mechanistic interpretation claims not specifically evaluated by peer reviewers.
